highlights.title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff
highlights.summary: Fears of more AI regulation appear to have sparked fear among investors, but concerns about the industry have been growing for some time.
body: Is the artificial intelligence (AI) gold rush coming to an end, or is this simply a reality check?
That's the question which is hanging over investors, and which has prompted steep falls on the world's stock markets.
The sell-off in the US on Thursday was most dramatic on the Nasdaq, home to tech industry titans such as Alphabet, Nvidia, Meta and Apple.
It followed sweeping gains by the Democrats in this week's midterm elections in the US, which have given the party full control of Congress.

highlights.title: AI is the new dating dealbreaker
highlights.summary: When Irene moved to San Francisco last year, she started using dating apps as a way to meet new people, get to know her new city, and connect with others who care about the things she does. After the 25-year-old analyst downloaded Hinge and started swiping, she noticed a trend.
body: Usually, the people who include this kind of value statement on their profile work in the arts, nursing, maybe graphic design. Within the span of a few minutes of sitting down and swiping, Irene shows me a second profile where this happened once more: “You should *not* go out with me if… you use AI.”

In San Francisco, the epicenter of tech, the metaphorical AI bomb went off in 2022 with the release of OpenAI’s ChatGPT. Conversations surrounding artificial intelligence now permeate the dating scene in one shape or another. Over the past month, I bopped around the city —, chatting with people at parties and coworking spaces and reviewing dating directories and other online profiles —, trying to find out how AI affects the dating scene.

highlights.title: Player-coach rift report will only galvanise England - George
highlights.summary: England hooker Jamie George says the squad are "really upset" by a newspaper article claiming the end of their summer tour was marked by player unrest over Steve Borthwick's leadership.
body: A report in the Times, external says unhappy players wanted summit talks with Borthwick and Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney in Argentina in July.

It alleges there are disagreements among Borthwick's wider coaching group, which has been subject to frequent change in his nearly four years in charge, and concerns over the head coach's man-management skills.
England meet Australia in the Nations Championship on Sunday at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham, with George querying the timing of the article as well as its contents.
The Saracens hooker, who was made England captain by Borthwick in 2024 before the role passed to Maro Itoje 12 months later, said that he did not recognise the situation described by the article.

highlights.title: David Staff obituary
highlights.summary: My former teacher and mentor David Staff, who has died aged 68 of a heart condition, was a cornetto player and period trumpeter, but also well known as a maker of natural trumpets – valveless brass instruments which, in the hands of a good player, produce a distinctive and rich sound.
body: The natural trumpet was the type of trumpet which, for many centuries, accompanied men and horses on the battlefield, but it was also admired by composers such as Bach and Handel, who both wrote music for it.

David got into making his instruments after meeting the natural trumpet maker Frank Tomes in the late 1980s. He learned a lot from Frank, and eventually became his apprentice in 2009, establishing his own workshop at his home near Coddenham in Suffolk. There he would make trumpets from flat sheets of brass: he shaped and soldered his tubes and drew them by hand, and created flared bell sections by hammering and swaging them into shape.

After Frank’s death David took over the business, with valuable input from his friend and fellow instrument maker, Graham Nicholson. Having served as David’s apprentice and hand engraver for 11 years, I will continue the workshop.

highlights.title: The folks behind John Wick are back with Karōshi trailer
highlights.summary: Those of us missing the John Wick universe can take heart, because Chad Stahelski—who created that franchise—is coming back early next year with a new dystopian action film.
body: Karōshi is an action-thriller set in a near-future Manhattan, where corporate loyalty and cultural tradition have reshaped everyday life. When a mysterious outsider infiltrates a powerful company after a worker’s death, he exposes the violent system hidden beneath its polished surface.

Teo Yoo (Past Lives) stars as the aptly named Hiro, who is clearly out for vengeance against the offending corporation. The cast also includes Takehiro Hira, so memorable in the 2024 miniseries Shōgun, as well as Giancarlo Esposito, Cynthia Erivo, Bill Camp, Richard Harmon, Isabel May, and Show Kasamatsu.

The trailer opens with Hira’s character lauding the contribution of Ikigai Technologies in helping shape “modern life for millions,” adding praise for employees’ “daily commitment and sacrifice.” Then we see one distraught worker deliberately falling backward to his death from the top of the company’s skyscraper. Enter our protagonist, Hiro, who suspects there is something more sinister going on behind the company’s embrace of the samurai path, marked by “integrity” and “honor”—and also violence.

highlights.title: AI Companies Really, Really Want to Buy Your Work Files and Emails
highlights.summary: Data brokers are collecting all sorts of internal corporate files to help train AI models. Not everyone is thrilled.
body: Lately a new kind of pitch has found its way into my inbox. “Not sure if you've heard,” writes someone named Nick, “but AI labs such as Anthropic and OpenAI are paying media companies such as Wired $350K to $1.8M as a one time fee for a copy of their old work records (documents, emails, slack messages, tickets, etc.) for training better models.”

Another email with a similar pitch (adding call transcripts to the list of desired information) raised the stakes to a possible $2 million. “Public data is exhausted, and the labs are spending over $45B on private data to build better models,” writes someone named Cora.

While I was aware that AI companies are buying expert data from various sources, there hasn’t been that much attention paid to it. But once I looked into it, I discovered that this business is way bigger than I suspected—and according to its practitioners, it could have as much impact on workers and society as the data centers that are dominating the news these days.

highlights.title: Scotland come full circle for another crack at All Blacks
highlights.summary: Sione Tuipulotu and Scotland have the chance to end one of sport's longest-standing hoodoos against New Zealand on Saturday, writes Andy Burke.
body: As Scotland prepare for their latest attempt at busting one of sport's longest standing hoodoos against the All Blacks on Saturday, it is worth reflecting on the journey this team has been on since their last tilt 12 months ago.

That match, in which Scotland fell 17-0 down, roared back to 17-17 all, only to succumb to the sorcery of Damien McKenzie late in the game, was another experience to file in Scottish rugby's bulging folder marked 'Ones That Got Away'.

It was a bitter disappointment, but worse was to follow when a 21-0 lead against Argentina spiralled into a nightmarish defeat that led to serious questions around the future of head coach Gregor Townsend.
The heat was turned up further still by a dispiriting loss to Italy in Rome to kick off this year's Six Nations. Since then, Scotland have flipped the narrative.

highlights.title: Xbox Series X | X25 Special Edition Console – Invite Requests Are Up at Amazon
highlights.summary: Back in August, when preorders went up for the translucent green Xbox Series X | X25 Special Edition console, they sold out almost instantly. That was a bummer for longtime Xbox fans who wanted to get their hands on one of these limited-edition 25th-anniversary consoles.
body: Requesting an invite doesn’t mean you’ll necessarily end up being invited to buy a console. But it gives you a chance to be invited, which is better than nothing. As Amazon says, “If invited to purchase, you’ll get an email when the item is available. Not all requests will be granted.”

The console is meant to celebrate the 25th anniversary of Xbox. It’s set to release on November 13 and costs (the curiously specific price) $909.23. Only 25,000 numbered consoles are being manufactured, which explains the difficulty people have had securing a preorder.

So what do you get if you do end up buying it? You get a 1TB Xbox Series X console, decked out in translucent green. The front of the console has an X25 logo, and when you turn it on, the X logo glows green as well. You also get a matching controller (which is also sold separately, and is still available at some retailers). Finally, you get a digital copy of Halo: Campaign Evolved, a remake of the campaign from the original Halo (see our review ).

highlights.title: You know the launch market is tough when satellite companies start building rockets
highlights.summary: There are optimistic plans for spaceflight, and then there are optimistic plans. AST SpaceMobile is a Texas-based, publicly traded company building very large satellites to provide direct-to-cell communications on Earth. But it has been having trouble finding rides to space.
body: “The Blacklift rocket is the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market, providing AST SpaceMobile with regular unconstrained access to orbit and providing for most favorable owner’s economics in the industry,” said Abel Avellan, founder, chairman, and CEO of AST SpaceMobile, in a news release.

To anyone with even a basic understanding of rockets, that timeline is wildly, fantastically, and stupidly optimistic. Still, the announcement is worth examining because it underscores two important trends in today’s launch industry.

First, it’s becoming increasingly apparent that satellite operators planning to deploy large constellations need to secure launch capacity years in advance, as Amazon did nearly half a decade ago. And if they can’t secure that capacity on favorable terms, they are now considering taking the extraordinary step of developing their own rockets.

body: Uncapped Paris FC forward Pablo Pagis was surprisingly summoned by France on Friday for Nations League matches against Turkey and Italy.

Pagis, 23, made the 23-man list after Paris Saint-Germain’s Maghnes Akliouche was ruled out by a calf injury. France coach Zinedine Zidane said Pagis has an “interesting” and “different profile” that he wants to assess.

Pagis joined Paris FC in the summer after Lorient stay in Ligue 1 following promotion the previous season. Last season Pagis, who can play across the front line, scored 10 goals in Ligue 1 and has two this campaign. Paris FC are currently fourth in the league, with former Chelsea manager Liam Rosenior making positive return to French football.
France tops their Nations league group with 10 points from four games and travel to Italy on 12 November before hosting Turkey three days later.

highlights.title: Dane Cook and Robert Bowling Announce Vicious Vocab, a Genre-Bending Word Game With a Big Twist
highlights.summary: Ex-Call of Duty creative strategist Robert Bowling and comedian Dane Cook have revealed a brand new genre-bending video game known as Vicious Vocab, exclusively to IGN.
body: Vicious Vocab is a genre-bending spin on casual word games like Scrabble, Words With Friends, and Wordle, with a big twist. While Bowling and Cook are careful not to share much about the twist to preserve some surprises, the game goes well beyond mixing and matching letters to make new words. The words have power and meaning… and they can dramatically change not only what happens to you, but the entire genre of game that you’re playing.
Check out the trailer below to get an idea of the unexpected shift that happens in Vicious Vocab.

Made by a team of five people who collectively call themselves “funcool games,” Vicious Vocab is described as “Scrabble meets Balatro in a backroom casino.” On its own, it’s a fun twist on the word game genre. There’s an action element, which has led the team to referring to the game as a “word brawler” or, in Cook’s words, a first-person speller.

highlights.title: ‘Wheel of Fortune’ Grows in Syndication and Streaming as Season 44 Introduces New Gameplay (EXCLUSIVE)
highlights.summary: “Wheel of Fortune” introduced some new features for its Season 44, and it appears to be paying off with viewers. The long-running syndicated game show is averaging 8.59 million viewers in linear this year, up 17% from last year, while its household rating is a 4.8, up 16% from last year.
body: In Season 44, “Wheel of Fortune” gameplay added a new opening round, dubbed “Fortune Frenzy,” which follows contestants as they’re given 30 seconds to solve as many puzzles as possible. That means more puzzles at the start of the show.

Sony said the ratings increase also comes as it assumes marketing, promotions and affiliate relations for “Wheel.” A year ago, CBS Media Ventures and Sony Pictures TV settled their long-running battle over the distribution of “Wheel” and “Jeopardy.” As part of their settlement, Sony took over international distribution of “Wheel” last year, while CBS kept domestic distribution through 2027-2028 (at which point Sony takes it over). CBS continued to handle marketing, promotions and affiliate relations last year, but all of that moved to Sony starting this fall.

highlights.title: Prince, the pope, and autumn 2026: purple is hot this season
highlights.summary: Spotted on Balenciaga, Celine and Valentino catwalks, purple is having a moment. If you really want to stand out, wear it with red. The colour purple has links to royalty, the Catholic church, Prince, Gordon Brown’s ties and Barney the dinosaur and it now has a new association – autumn 2026.
body: It has been deemed fashion’s favourite colour having been spotted on autumn/winter catwalks, with Balenciaga, Celine and Valentino showcasing all-purple designs.

Jennifer Lawrence and Zoë Kravitz have also been spotted wearing purple, while Naomi Ackie and Nicola Peltz have worn it on the red carpet. The high street is in on the trend too, with Cos, H&M and Asos selling purple knitwear and accessories.

This season’s shade has been called “royal purple” – a vivid take on the colour, rather than a darker plum or muted lilac. This is a contrast to the neutrals that have dominated fashion in recent years.
In fact, fashion insiders are leaning into the bright theme by often pairing purple with red. Vogue recently declared that autumn’s “coolest colour clash” had arrived.

highlights.title: Meta’s Muse AI can create custom ‘spaces’ for the version of the app you need right now
highlights.summary: Meta will now allow you to build customized, app-like experiences within its Muse AI assistant. The new feature, called "spaces," allows Muse to build things like a shopping hub, school dashboard, music tracker, trivia game, and more, which you can interact with directly in the app.
body: You can create things like a shopping hub, school dashboard, or music tracker directly within Muse.

If you connect your space to a relevant app, Muse will update pricing, dates, and other information in the background. Meta says you can create a new space by describing it, and continue to tweak it by asking Muse. You can also interact with your spaces by checking things off, adding notes, and making edits.

You can add spaces to the sidebar in the Muse app, move them into your main tab, as well as schedule when you see them. “For example, keep your weekly planner up front during the workweek, then swap it for your weekend plans on Saturday,” Meta says.

Meta is rolling out spaces to all Muse users, along with a “specialized” version of its Muse Wonder AI model. The company is also looking into ways to share your spaces with other users and collaborate with them.

body: The Times reported that some England players lost faith in Borthwick during a summer campaign with included a 45-21 defeat to world champions South Africa and a nervy win over Argentina.

It is alleged players objected to Borthwick's treatment of them, that he was involved in a training ground bust-up with Ellis Genge and that they wanted RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney - who this week unequivocally backed the head coach - to listen to their gripes.

Speaking to Sky Sports News on Friday, hooker George, captain for the July tour with Maro Itoje rested and named in the starting XV to face the Wallabies this weekend, says the squad addressed the article and will use it to "galavanise" them.

The 36-year-old, who insisted England are "all massively behind Steve in every way possible" said: "I'm really disappointed with the article that's been written. There's not a huge amount of truth to any of it, really.

highlights.title: Protesters break into Microsoft data center site in Amsterdam
highlights.summary: Protesters have broken into a construction site of a new Microsoft data center in Amsterdam this morning. Members of the Geef Tegengas group helped organize the protest against the construction of three 85-meter data center towers in the outskirts of Amsterdam.
body: Reuters reports that around 100 people made it into the construction site, with some scaling a crane to place a “fuck AI” banner. Protesters also unfurled a “Microsoft powers genocide” banner on the construction site, and chanted “Microsoft has got to go” and “free Palestine.”

Opposition to the new data center in Amsterdam comes more than a year after the city banned new data centers until 2030, after a temporary stop that was announced at the end of 2023. Microsoft will be the sole tenant of this new data center, and the project is proceeding as it was planned as far back as 2016, before a ban was put in place. The site, being built by British developer Pure Data Centres, has also managed to navigate some loopholes to reach the construction stage.

highlights.title: Mass Effect Is Getting A New Art Collection At A Difficult Time For Its Fans
highlights.summary: This year's annual Mass Effect Day looks to be somber in light of the studio behind the games, BioWare, being shut down last month. But while no new Mass Effect games are currently on the horizon, you can celebrate its legacy through some classy art prints that are going up for sale ahead of N7…
body: Moor-Art says it began collaborating with BioWare over a year ago to release a new selection of limited-edition posters. "What began as a celebration of an ongoing saga now feels like the bastion in the continuation of a studio's legacy," the studio said in a press release.

The collection from Moor-Art is inspired by the characters and worlds of Mass Effect, with the original artwork being produced by acclaimed artists and Mass Effect die-hard fans Matt Essom and Dan Mumford. The designs will also be available as T-shirts. The first one is by Essom, and Moor-Art says this illustration captures the spirit and emotional depth of the series, as well as the bonds forged on the Normandy as her crew traveled to unknown worlds. This will be limited to 200 hand-numbered prints worldwide, plus 30 Giclée prints with a certificate of authenticity signed by the artist.

highlights.title: George R.R. Martin Tapped for Lifetime Achievement Nod at Infinity Festival (Exclusive)
highlights.summary: In addition, Pola Maneli, director of the animated short 'Apart,' co-written by Spike Lee, has joined the lineup for the previously announced ASIFA-Showcase.
body: George R.R. Martin has been tapped to receive the Monolith Lifetime Achievement Award at this year’s Infinity Festival.

Martin, creator of the A Song of Ice and Fire novels that inspired HBO’s Game of Thrones, will accept the award at the event, which is set to take place Nov. 12-15 at the Audrey Irmas Pavilion in Los Angeles.

Heirs of the Perisphere, directed by Chris Eyre and written by Caroline Spector, is based on a short story by Martin’s longtime friend, science-fiction author Howard Waldrop. The film follows three animatronic robots who awaken after centuries of silence to discover humanity has vanished and embark on a journey to find their creators.

The Monolith Lifetime Achievement Award recognizes “individuals whose contributions have left a lasting impact on entertainment,” organizers said. The festival will honor Martin’s “lifetime of storytelling and his dedication to bringing the work of his dear friend Howard Waldrop to the screen.”

highlights.title: Martine Rose appointed creative director at Balenciaga
highlights.summary: Fashion house move marks breakthrough in white, male-dominated industry. For the first time in its 109-year history, the fashion house Balenciaga is to be led by a woman, with the British designer Martine Rose appointed as creative director of the brand.
body: Her appointment at Balenciaga marks a breakthrough in the white, male-dominated fashion industry. Rose is only the second Black woman to lead a major European house. Her appointment follows Grace Wales Bonner, who in 2025 was announced as the men’s creative director at Hermès.

Rose, who launched her own label in London in 2007, has become one of the most influential voices in menswear. She has built a cult following for her streetwear-inspired designs and celebrations of British subcultures through her mashup of influences including football, reggae and northern soul.

Her designs have been worn by celebrities including Justin Bieber, Timothée Chalamet and Drake. Alongside namechecking her in a song, the rapper Kendrick Lamar turned to Rose for a custom varsity jacket, emblazoned with Gloria, one of his song titles, for his widely acclaimed 2025 Super Bowl half-time performance. Rihanna and Hailey Bieber are also fans.
She succeeds Pierpaolo Piccioli, whose departure was announced on Thursday after 18 months at the luxury Spanish brand.

highlights.title: “Does Meta think we can’t read?” Meta abandons sketchy commercial terms update.
highlights.summary: After weeks of backlash —and a failed attempt to quell it —Meta has indefinitely delayed plans to update its commercial terms and require Meta Business account users to allow extensive AI training on external websites linked on Facebook.
body: “We’re pausing the ‌changes ⁠as we continue to engage with stakeholders and ​take ​our ⁠time to get this right. ​In the ​meantime, ⁠our existing terms remain in ⁠effect,” a Meta spokesperson told Reuters.

Soon after Meta notified business account holders of the upcoming changes, legal experts warned Nieman Lab that the vague language could allow the company to ignore scraping preferences specified in robots.txt files and exhaustively crawl vast amounts of off-Facebook content for AI training. Since virtually every news publisher has a Facebook page, Nieman Lab sounded the alarm that Meta could potentially avoid millions in licensing fees if the TOS update happened as planned.

Ars broke down the changes after Meta announced them, noting that businesses—including news publishers involved in drawn-out legal battles over unwanted AI scraping—had no way to opt out. To keep a business Facebook page, they had to allow Meta to crawl any linked external sites. The terms even required publishers to create test credentials so Meta’s bots could reliably bypass paywalls.

highlights.title: Autism, masking, and building a more inclusive world | Letters
highlights.summary: Readers respond to an article by John Harris on the rise in the number of people labelled autistic over the last 20 years. John Harris’s article addresses all the main issues that are being debated around autism ( ‘The term is becoming unrecognisable’: have the experts who believed in a single…
body: From a young age I sensed that I was experiencing the world differently to other people. I was bullied, and worked hard to fit in. I was fortunate as structurally I had a stable life that mitigated some of the more challenging aspects of my life. Things started to get less manageable when I entered adulthood and left home.

Since the age of 25 I have experienced bouts of depression and ongoing anxiety, often resulting in breakdowns, or what I now understand to be autistic burnouts. Throughout adulthood I have seen numerous medical professionals and repeatedly been directed towards therapies, designed to deal with anxiety and depression, which have had limited success in addressing my life challenges.

Despite having a postgraduate education, I have struggled to hold down many jobs and have had to leave most due to stress. I have ongoing relationship problems. I don’t have children, partly due to reluctance and health issues. I suffer from fatigue and sleep issues.
